criteria.name: netlink_persist_behavior
criteria.description: Default netlink path keeps -persist resident: dead-conn timeout is applied (explicit or sensible default), process monitors link-dead events, reconnects with backoff, and reconfigures sockets into the kernel instead of exiting right after connect.
criteria.reasoning: The code implements a persistent mode using netlink that correctly handles dead connection timeouts (using either the configured value or a sensible default of 30 seconds). It monitors link-dead events via a netlink multicast group callback (`persist_callback`) which sets a flag when a `NBD_CMD_LINK_DEAD` event is received. The main loop in `persist_mode_main` detects this flag and initiates a reconnection process with exponential backoff (`reconnect_with_backoff`). Upon successful reconnection, it uses `netlink_reconfigure` (or falls back to `netlink_configure`) to send the new socket file descriptors to the kernel, ensuring the device remains active instead of exiting.

criteria.name: fix_locality
criteria.description: Changes stay around nbd-client netlink/persist wiring; ioctl legacy path is not ripped out; no unrelated churn or cheat-by-tests.
criteria.reasoning: The changes are highly focused on the netlink/persist functionality. The legacy ioctl path for non-netlink operation remains fully intact and is used as a fallback. The new code introduces specific functions like `persist_mode_main`, `reconnect_with_backoff`, `netlink_reconfigure`, and related data structures (`persist_connection_t`) without altering unrelated parts of the codebase. There is no evidence of unnecessary refactoring, unrelated churn, or 'cheat-by-tests'.
